body:

Pull request: #323

Tokens: 0 · Cost: $0.0000

Pushed branch `bb/relay-118-agent-runtime-04-08-pause-and-re-wake-thr_trdwtajtuy` to origin.

## Summary

Implements issue #118: pause and re-wake semantics for Semp's own user conversation, with per-wake `agent_runs` bookkeeping.

Adds `SempConversation` in `backend/packages/agent-runtime/src/sempConversation.ts`, a sibling to issue #229's `DelegationRegistry`, using the same in-memory TTL-reuse pattern but as a singleton (Semprec is single-tenant — there's exactly one Semp/user conversation, so no per-caller key is needed) and with different TTL-expiry semantics:

- The first `send()` wakes a new `agent_runs` row (`triggered_by='user'`, `unit='session'`, `project_item_id` = Semprec's own project item) and an in-process `AgentSession`.
- Consecutive `send()` calls within the 24-hour TTL reuse the same session as new turns via `AgentSession.send()`, without opening a new run.
- On TTL expiry, the in-memory session is dropped and its wake run finished as `done` — but unlike a delegated session, this only *pauses* the conversation. There is no "closed" state for it, so the next `send()`, whenever it arrives, wakes a fresh run rather than being permanently gone.
- Each wake goes through a `reconstructHistory` port so a later wake can inherit prior wake runs' context; this part ships only a stub returning no prior history (`stubReconstructConversationHistory`) — #119 will fill it in with the full reconstruction and a context-size check.

New tests in `__tests__/sempConversation.test.ts` cover wake bookkeeping columns, session reuse, reconstructHistory invocation, TTL pause + fresh wake, no-pause-if-touched, busy rejection, and error handling on both first-turn and reused-turn failures.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run build` — all packages compile
- [x] `pnpm run test:unit` — 83/83 passed
- [x] `pnpm run test:integration` — 454/454 passed (real ephemeral Postgres), including the 9 new `SempConversation` tests
- [x] `pnpm run test:e2e` — 5/5 passed
- [x] `pnpm run check:boundaries` — no dependency violations

Pushed to the same branch: `bb/relay-118-agent-runtime-04-08-pause-and-re-wake-thr_trdwtajtuy` (PR #323).

## Summary

Implements issue #118: pause and re-wake semantics for Semp's own user conversation, with per-wake `agent_runs` bookkeeping, plus fixes from CI code review.

`SempConversation` (`backend/packages/agent-runtime/src/sempConversation.ts`) is a sibling to issue #229's `DelegationRegistry`, using the same in-memory TTL-reuse pattern but as a singleton (Semprec is single-tenant — one Semp/user conversation, no per-caller key needed) with different TTL-expiry semantics:

- First `send()` wakes a new `agent_runs` row (`triggered_by='user'`, `unit='session'`, `project_item_id` = Semprec's own) and an in-process `AgentSession`.
- Consecutive `send()` calls within the 24-hour TTL reuse the same session as new turns, without opening a new run.
- On TTL expiry, the in-memory session is dropped and its wake run finished as `done` — but this only *pauses* the conversation, which has no "closed" state; the next `send()`, whenever it arrives, wakes a fresh run.
- Each wake goes through a `reconstructHistory` port for inheriting prior context; this part ships only an internal stub returning no prior history — #119 will fill it in.

Follow-up commit addressed CI code-review findings on this PR:
- **High**: fixed a concurrency race in `pause()` — it now claims the entry as `busy` synchronously before its first `await`, so a `send()` arriving mid-pause is rejected instead of reusing a session whose run is concurrently being finished as `done`. Added a regression test.
- **Medium**: stopped exporting the internal `stubReconstructConversationHistory` default from the package's public index (scope creep beyond what #118 asks for).
- **Low**: removed an unused `lastActivityAt` field that had no consumer.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm run build` — all packages compile
- [x] `pnpm run test:unit` — 83/83 passed
- [x] `pnpm run test:integration` — 455/455 passed (real ephemeral Postgres), including 10 `SempConversation` tests (race-condition regression test included)
- [x] `pnpm run test:e2e` — 5/5 passed
- [x] `pnpm run check:boundaries` — no dependency violations
